design.question: When an importer cuts its MFN applied tariff on an HS6 product by at least 2 percentage points, how does the value of its imports of that product (from all exporters) change over the following years, relative to the same importer's products that were on similar import paths and whose MFN rate had not yet changed, allowing one year of anticipation?

treatment.absorbing: later changes are part of the post-period path
treatment.concordance_rule: HS2022 reporting years enter only for HS2022 codes that correspond one-to-one, in both directions, to an HS2017 code in the UN correlation table (4,097 codes); when a reporter publishes both revisions for a year the HS2017 rate is used
treatment.definition: cohort g = reporting year of the unit's first MFN change of at least 0.5 pp in absolute value between consecutive reported years, when that first change is a decrease of at least 2.0 pp
treatment.design_stage_counts: Universe 264,038 reporter x HS2017 units with a 2018 rate (49 reporters): 238,631 never changed, 10,509 first changes are decreases of at least 2 pp, 12,460 other first changes, 2,438 first changes span a reporting gap. With a one-to-one HS1992 code: 6,520 decrease units (2019: 1,961; 2020: 1,582; 2021: 2,173; 2022: 569; 2023: 235) and 147,920 never-changed units, before the positive-import requirements. Largest reporters of decrease units: PAK 1,252, CHN 1,123, LKA 925, GBR 655, ECU 447, KAZ 397.
treatment.excluded_units: units whose first change is an increase or a decrease under 2.0 pp, and units whose first change spans a gap in the reporter's reporting years (timing unknown)
treatment.never_treated: units with an HS2017 rate reported for 2018 and no change of at least 0.5 pp between any consecutive reported years (censored when the reporter stops reporting or a code has no one-to-one HS2022 counterpart)
treatment.source: wits_trains_tariffs MFN simple-average applied rates (not the event library, which keeps only same-revision changes), mapped to HS2017 codes

units.definition: importer (WITS reporter with an ISO3 code that is a BACI importer) x HS2017 HS6 product with a one-to-one HS1992 code
units.sample: positive BACI HS1992 import value in 2009, 2013 and 2017
units.strata: importer x tercile of log import growth 2009-2013 (terciles within importer by (growth, id) rank): every comparison is within the importing country and growth tercile

overall.definition: equal-weight mean of ATT(e) over the post event times listed

assumptions: Parallel trends: absent treatment, the average outcome of treated units would have moved like that of the comparison units (not-yet-treated or never-treated, within stratum when stratified) from the base period on.
No anticipation beyond the registered anticipation window: outcomes before g - anticipation do not respond.
Absorbing treatment: the first qualifying event defines the cohort; later events are part of the post-period treatment path, so estimates are effects of entering treatment, not of one isolated event.
SUTVA / no interference: a unit's outcome does not depend on other units' treatment (spillovers to comparison units bias the estimate toward zero or away from it).
Treatment timing is recorded correctly by the source date the registration names.
Within an importer and a 2009-2013 import-growth tercile, which products receive an MFN cut first is unrelated to product-specific import trends after 2013.
Anticipation lasts at most one year: imports before g-1 do not respond to the cut.
MFN rates bind for a material share of imports; preferential partners dilute the effect toward zero. The estimate is on total imports.
One-to-one concordance codes measure the same goods in HS2017, HS2022 and HS1992; restricting to them selects products whose definitions did not change, which may not represent all products.
No interference: substitution into neighbouring comparison products of the same importer is small.
Reporters that stop reporting censor treatment; a unit recorded as never treated may have changed later.
identification.estimand: ATT: equal-weight mean over event times 0..3 of treated-count-weighted ATT(g, g+e), base period g-2
identification.label: did_failed_diagnostics
identification.meaning: A difference-in-differences estimate whose pre-registered diagnostics failed. It is reported for transparency and must not be read as an intervention response.

results.verdict: No causal claim. Pre-registered diagnostics failed (no_pre_trends, placebo_date_null), so the parallel-trends design is not credible here. The estimate for log import value from all exporters (BACI HS1992, thousand current USD), -0.0072 log points (95% CI -0.0558 to +0.0414), is reported only for transparency.

identification.label: quasi_experimental_did
identification.meaning: Average effect on the treated identified by a staggered difference-in-differences design whose pre-registered diagnostics (pre-trends, placebo dates, placebo units) all passed. Causal only under the stated assumptions, for the treated population and horizon studied.

results.verdict: Diagnostics passed; the effect on log import quantity from all exporters (BACI HS1992, metric tons; cells with any flow lacking quantity dropped) is a null: -0.0090 log points (95% CI -0.0896 to +0.0717). The design rules out average effects outside that interval under the stated assumptions.
